note: The radar signature treatments (ADR-30, MS-3): one set of values for every aircraft. An aircraft takes each treatment its own documentation states it has (aircraft/<type>/signature.json), whatever its origin. Nothing is fitted to any aircraft's claimed RCS: the published figures check the result, they do not set it.

ram_full_loss_db.note: a skin coated all over with radar-absorbent material: its specular returns lowered by this much at 4 GHz and above. Chung et al. find a bare F-22 CAD model at about 10 dBsm nose on and 0 to -10 dBsm off it, and -10 to -20 dBsm with RAM in the desired direction: 10-20 dB, its middle. A practical 6.25 mm layer gives more than 10 dB from 4 to 18 GHz (sutrakar-2025).
ram_full_loss_db.evidence: With RAM applied, the RCS can be reduced to the level of -10 ~ -20 dBsm in desired direction and frequency band

ram_partial_loss_db.note: radar-absorbent material on the largest reflectors only (leading edges, intake lips): a fraction of the full coating's effect, taken as half the frontal skin's returns treated

ram_low_frequency.note: below this a coating's loss falls in proportion to the frequency (assumed: a layer thin against the wavelength); from it upwards its full loss
ram_low_frequency.evidence: more than -10 dB reflection loss from 4 to 18GHz

intake_concealed_loss_db.note: an intake whose curvature (a serpentine duct, vanes, a blocker) hides the engine face: its cavity's return lowered by this much at 9.5 GHz; less at lower frequencies, as (f / 9.5 GHz)^0.3 - about 11 dB at 3 GHz, as an MLFMM study of an S-shaped inlet is reported to find (10-12 dB at 3 GHz, about 16 at 10 GHz; a search summary, its paper not identified)
intake_concealed_loss_db.evidence: The modified design mean RCS reduction is about 16.94 dBsm
